list.title: Consumers
list.show_all: Show every consumer, even without power

view.off_in_period: Averages only apply to the kW view

energy.filled: {percent} of the time filled in from neighbouring values
energy.rest: Includes filled-in, later or missing consumer values
energy.late: Statistics only from {date}; the period counts from then
energy.no_statistics: Energy mode: not every main sensor (solar, grid, battery, house) has long-term statistics; the card stays with power.

config.missing_entities: {field} is missing: at least three of the four balance quantities must be configured as sensors.
config.mixed_form: {field}: use either an entity id, the entity/invert form, the two-entity form or derived - not a mixture.
config.two_derived: Only one balance quantity may be derived; {field} would be the second one.
config.soc_without_battery: {field} has no effect without entities.battery and is ignored.
config.soc_stops: {field} needs at least two stops in ascending order, the first at 0 and the last at 100.
config.soc_stop_entry: {field} needs a numeric at value and a colour.
config.consumer_entity: {field} has no entity and is skipped.
config.duplicate_consumer: {field}: entity {entity} is listed more than once; the later entry is skipped.
config.solar_house: {field}: only "excluded" (not part of the house value) is allowed; the value is ignored.
config.pv_scale: {field}: "% kWp" needs kwp on every source, "100%" at least two sources; the card uses what is possible.
config.order_fixed: {first} must be less than {second} - {second} was raised to {value}.
config.clamped: {field} must be between {min} and {max} - {value} is used.
config.grid_status_no_outage: {field} needs an entity and at least one outage state - without them the grid status is ignored.
config.empty_choice: {field}: an empty list counts as not set; the default applies.
config.energy_derived: {field}: the energy mode does not work with a derived grid or battery; it stays off.
config.charge_no_soc: {field} has no soc entity and is ignored.
config.charge_no_plugged: {field}: show plugged needs a plugged entity - listed by power instead.
config.condition_incomplete: {field} needs an entity, an operator and a value - shown by power until then.
config.condition_number: {field}: {operator} compares with exactly one number - the condition is never met.
config.show_twice: {field}: show and charge.show are both set - show is used, charge.show ignored.
config.extra_no_entity: {field} has no entity and is ignored.
config.not_for_node: {field} does not exist for this node and is ignored.
config.order_used: {field}: to keep the order, the card uses {value}.
config.clamped_min: {field} must be at least {min} - {value} is used.
config.unknown_value: {field}: unknown value, allowed are {allowed} - the card uses the default.

editor.title: Title
editor.name: Name
editor.yaml_only: Only editable in YAML - the values there are not in a form this editor can show.
editor.grid_status_ok: States that mean: grid is there
editor.dot_color_follow: Dots in the colour of their line
editor.arrow_colors_red_green: Arrows red/green: import and discharge red, export and charge green (otherwise in their direction's colour) - in energy mode and the detail window
editor.colors_hint: Colours are set further down, in the group “Colours”.
editor.note_order_avg_short_minutes: The short window must be shorter than the long one.
editor.note_order_avg_long_minutes: The long window must be longer than the short one.
editor.note_order_fast_s: The fast cycle must be shorter than the slow one.
editor.note_order_slow_s: The slow cycle must be longer than the fast one.
editor.note_order_min_w: Must lie below the thresholds for the dots.
editor.note_order_slow_below_w: The thresholds must grow from top to bottom.
editor.note_order_more_dots_above_w: The thresholds must grow from top to bottom.
editor.note_order_max_dots_at_w: The thresholds must grow from top to bottom.
editor.note_order_full_speed_w: Must be above the threshold for slow dots.
editor.pv_source_excluded: Not part of the house value

editor_help.min_consumer_w: Consumers below this power are hidden and counted towards the remainder. Default: 10 W.
editor_help.max_consumers: Only the strongest consumers are listed; the rest are counted together. Empty = all (default).
editor_help.update_interval_s: How often the list reorders. The figures themselves update immediately. Default: 5 seconds.
editor_help.rest_label: Name for the part that is not measured individually. Default: "Other".
editor_help.design: How the travelling dots look. “Plain dots” is a circle and nothing else; the others give it a lighter core and, depending on the design, a glow. Speed and the number of dots follow the power, not the design. Default: plain dots.
editor_help.dot_size: 100 % is the size of the dots on a card with large nodes. Smaller cards - the list beside the drawing, a phone - take somewhat smaller dots on their own. Default: 100 %.
editor_help.line_width: 100 % is 3 px for the connections and 2 px for the lines to the list on a card with large nodes. Smaller cards take somewhat thinner lines on their own. Default: 100 %.
editor_help.avg_short_minutes: Window for the short average. Default: 2.
editor_help.avg_long_minutes: Window for the long average. Default: 15.
editor_help.energy_periods: What the quick button offers: power, and energy over a period worked out from the statistics of the power sensors. Several ticked: each tap steps on. One ticked: fixed, no button. Default: power, today, 24 h, week – but only when solar, grid, battery and house have statistics, otherwise power alone. Grid and battery with two sensors show both directions; with one signed sensor the grid shows its balance and the battery no figure.
editor_help.energy_periods_locked: Not available with a derived grid or battery.
editor_help.inactive_lines: Connections with nothing flowing on them. "Hide" calms the picture at night. Default: show.
editor_help.animation: "Follow system setting" respects the device's reduce-motion preference - that lives in the operating system, not in Home Assistant. Default: follow system setting.
editor_help.ring_animation: How the consumer ring follows a reordered list. “Overtake”: every segment travels to its new place, one moving forward passes on an inner lane. “Cross-fade colours”: the places stay, their colours blend into the new order. “Jump”: no motion, new values show at once. With Motion off the ring always jumps. Default: overtake.
editor_help.battery_soc: State of charge in percent. Never averaged.
editor_help.color: Any CSS value, e.g. #7e57c2 or var(--primary-color). Empty = automatic.
editor_help.solar: Positive = production. If the sensor reports production as negative, flip the sign.
editor_help.grid: Positive = import from the grid, negative = export. If your sensor has it the other way round, flip the sign.
editor_help.house: Total consumption of the house. Without a sensor of its own, choose "Derived".
editor_help.battery: Positive = discharging, negative = charging (Home Assistant's convention). If your sensor has it the other way round, flip the sign.
editor_help.battery_charge: Charging from all sources, as a magnitude ≥ 0.
editor_help.derived: Calculated from the other three quantities so the balance adds up. Only one quantity can be derived.
editor_help.min_w: From this power on a connection counts as active: dots move, grid and battery show their state. Below it everything is neutral. Default: 10 W.
editor_help.icon_battery: Empty = icon follows the state of charge.
editor_help.peak_w: One value for the whole motion: at this power the most dots run at their fastest. The three thresholds below derive from it (1/12, 1/3, 1/1) while they are empty. Default 6000 W.
editor_help.flow_fine: Only needed when the peak power alone does not do. A set value overrides the one derived from the peak. If the order is wrong, the card raises the second value and says so in the browser console.
editor_help.slow_below_w: Below this a single dot runs at resting pace. From here on it gets faster. Default: peak / 12.
editor_help.more_dots_above_w: From here on more dots join, independent of the speed. Default: peak / 3.
editor_help.max_dots_at_w: From here on as many dots as allowed. In between: more and more dots. Default: peak.
editor_help.slow_s: One lap when little is flowing. Default 5.
editor_help.fast_s: One lap when a lot is flowing. Default 1.8.
editor_help.max_dots: How many dots a connection carries at most. Default 5.
editor_help.full_speed_w: From here on the dot runs as fast as it gets. In between: one dot, getting faster. Default: same as “More dots from”.
editor_help.power_unit: Kilowatts, watts or automatic. “Automatic” picks per value: whole watts below 1000 W, kilowatts above - otherwise a 30 W consumer reads as “0.0 kW”. Default: kilowatts.
editor_help.power_decimals: Kilowatts only; watts are always whole numbers. Default 2.
editor_help.grid_status: Only if your installation reports an outage - many do not. Without it the card shows no outage; everything else works.
editor_help.grid_status_outage: Required. Every integration names its states differently, so nothing is guessed here. Enter the raw state, not the label Home Assistant shows: an enum sensor displays a translated name, so “Not detected” may really be `not_detected`. Picking from the list avoids the question.
editor_help.grid_status_ok: Optional. Left empty, the entity's own options minus the outage states count as \u201cgrid is there\u201d; anything else, including unavailable, leaves the last state standing.
editor_help.layout: Where the four nodes stand. With Square · solar left the PV rows stand left of the drawing and the consumers right of it; on a card too narrow for that, both lists go below. Default: Cross.
editor_help.flow_lines: How the connections between the nodes run. Default: curved for the cross, straight for the other arrangements.
editor_help.appearance: Shows this one card light or dark – whatever the theme says, and without touching the rest of the dashboard. It also settles which of its two value sets a flow design takes. “Follow the theme” reads the ground, which works nearly always – but not for themes that paint no card background of their own. Light and dark use Home Assistant's default colours, not those of a custom theme.
editor_help.dot_color: Empty = each dot carries the colour of its flow, which is what shows where the energy comes from. A colour here applies to every dot on the card; the lines keep theirs.
editor_help.power_digits: How much the number says, not how many places follow the point. With 3: 1.23 kW · 12.3 kW · 123 kW. A decimal place means something different at 1.23 kW than at 123 kW; this keeps what the figure tells constant. Watts are always whole. Default: 3.
editor_help.consumers_list: Unfold to edit, drag by the handle to sort. The colour is under “Colours”.
editor_help.consumer_min_w: Overrides the global minimum power - say 50 W for a heat pump, so its standby does not count as a consumer.
editor_help.consumer_soc: For a wallbox, the car’s state of charge from the car’s own integration. Shown as a ring around the icon; while nothing charges it stands in the row instead of the power.
editor_help.consumer_label: An own name instead of “State of charge”, when the value is something else in percent. Shown in the tooltip and the detail window. Empty: state of charge.
editor_help.consumer_show: From its minimum power a consumer is always listed. 'Always' or a condition keep it there as well, even at 0 W - a wallbox while the car is plugged in, say. Held rows count towards the maximum number of consumers.
editor_help.node_show_state: Without the state word only the colour tells export from import, charging from discharging.
editor_help.node_inside_entity: Any entity. The circle only has room for a number and its unit. Always shows the current state, also in the average views.
editor_help.node_label_entity: Any entity, right next to the circle. Always shows the current state, also in the average views.
editor_help.node_label_prefix: Free text in front of the value, e.g. "Self-sufficiency".
editor_help.node_inside_decimals: "As in Home Assistant" uses the display precision from the entity's settings. Significant digits apply whatever the unit: 1.23 · 12.3 · 123. Text, money, durations and points in time are not affected - they always look as in Home Assistant.
editor_help.node_label_decimals: "As in Home Assistant" uses the display precision from the entity's settings. Significant digits apply whatever the unit: 1.23 · 12.3 · 123. Text, money, durations and points in time are not affected - they always look as in Home Assistant.
editor_help.node_inside_size: In percent of the node value.
editor_help.node_label_size: In percent of the label (12 px).
editor_help.node_inside_position: Above the icon the value sits where the battery shows its charge, and tapping it opens its own history. Below the value, tapping opens the node's entity.
editor_help.modes: What the quick button offers: now, the short and the long average. Several ticked: each tap steps on. One ticked: fixed, no button. Default: all three.
editor_help.modes_locked: Averages exist for power only. Tick “Power” under “Quick button power/energy” to set the smoothing. Until then the card always shows the current reading.
editor_help.scope: What the quick button offers: the filtered consumer list or every consumer. Several ticked: each tap switches. One ticked: fixed, no button. Default: both.
editor_help.list_enabled: Default: on when consumers are set.
editor_help.ring_enabled: Ring of the consumers at the house. Default: on when consumers are set.
editor_help.list_always_below: Keeps the list under the drawing even when there is room beside it. Default: off.
editor_help.quick_buttons: The buttons in the card's header. For each, what it offers: several values – each tap steps on; one value – fixed, no button.
editor_help.solar_sources: Every inverter or string with a sensor of its own; the PV is their sum. A source's colour can be set in YAML (color), otherwise orange tones.
editor_help.pv_source_kwp: Needed on every source for the "% kWp" scale. Default: none.
editor_help.pv_source_excluded: For sources feeding in past the inverter (balcony plant): their power is added to the measured house value. Default: off.
editor_help.list_solar: Shows each source as a row above the consumers, with a fan of its own. Default: off.
editor_help.ring_solar: Ring of the sources at the PV node. Default: on.
editor_help.pv_scales: What the quick button offers: "100%" - the ring shows each source's share and is always full; "% kWp" - the power relative to peak power. Several ticked: each tap switches. One ticked: fixed, no button. Default: both, as far as possible.
editor_help.pv_scale_peak_locked: "% kWp" needs the peak power (kWp) of every source. Enter it under "PV sources" to choose this scale.
editor_help.pv_scale_share_locked: "100%" needs at least two sources - with one the ring would always be full.
editor_help.quick_style: How the quick buttons look. "Segment buttons, compact" also makes the cycling buttons flatter; "Single buttons" shows with expanded quick buttons. Default: segment buttons.
editor_help.expanded_modes: Every value as its own button side by side instead of one button that cycles. Default: off.
editor_help.expanded_energy_periods: Every value as its own button side by side instead of one button that cycles. Default: off.
editor_help.expanded_pv_scales: Every value as its own button side by side instead of one button that cycles. Default: off.
editor_help.expanded_scope: Filtered and Complete as two buttons instead of one filter button. Default: off.
editor_help.consumer_position: Top/bottom gives a consumer a fixed position in the list. With several consumers at the top/bottom, the order of the consumer list here in the editor decides as well.
editor_help.condition_values: One or more states; = means 'is one of them', ≠ 'is none of them'. Numbers are compared as numbers.
editor_help.condition_number: One number, in the sensor's unit.
editor_help.consumers_held_limit: {held} consumers are shown always or by a condition, the maximum is {limit}. No other consumer appears then.
